findings.summary: The doc says unmodeled-markdown detection exists to surface an agent skill's `SKILL.md`, but `unmodeled_markdown` skips any file whose stem is a conventional doc name, and `"skill"` is in that set — so `SKILL.md` files are never reported as unmodeled.
findings.evidence: Doc: "two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references). Neither has a code sibling, so neither can move the percentage". Code (`unmodeled_markdown`): `if os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(md))[0].lower() in CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS: continue  # README/CHANGELOG/… are docs, not an unmodeled corpus`, with `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS = {..., "code_of_conduct", "skill", "todo", ...}`. A repo of three skills each consisting of a single `SKILL.md` therefore yields `unmodeled == []` (only non-`SKILL` references are counted, as in AC-4).
findings.suggestion: Either drop `"skill"` from the stem filter used by `unmodeled_markdown` (keep it only for the orphan check, e.g. pass a separate conventional-doc set per call site), or amend the doc's rationale to say only a skill's *reference* markdown is surfaced and `SKILL.md` itself is treated as a conventional doc.

verification.doc_quote: **Why:** two real bodies of writing are invisible to a same-stem model — a spec tree keyed by requirement id (`spec/functional/FR-021-….md`) and behavior implemented AS markdown (an agent skill's `SKILL.md` and its references).
verification.why: The only line mentioning `SKILL.md` in this section is the "Why:" rationale explaining why such writing is invisible to same-stem pairing, not a claim about which files the detector reports; the section's normative sentence — "A file qualifies when it sits in a directory holding no candidate code, is not user-excluded, and is not a conventional doc name" — matches the code's `CONVENTIONAL_DOC_STEMS` skip exactly.
